text:
support_jess: @customer_ops thanks for the ticket — can you confirm this is happening for the EU dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-eu-42)? You mentioned increased latency and a billing bump.
customer_ops: yes, started ~2026-02-14 13:02 UTC. Sample req IDs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e. 95th latency jumped to ~850ms and we saw fallback to hosted.
support_jess: do you have the exact route header from a failing response? we need the routed_region and pool tags.
customer_ops: here's a full response header from one: 
```
x-routed-region: eu-west-1
x-served-pool: hosted-us-east-1
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
x-fallback-reason: pool_unavailable
```
infra_dan: that x-served-pool looks wrong. If routed_region=eu-west-1 we should be serving from ded-eu-42, not hosted-us-east-1. possible pin mismatch or TTL expiry.
oncall_maya: I'm running a quick repro against the customer's pinned route. curl command: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <cust-token>" -H "x-customer-id: cust-877" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1"
```
Got 200 but response headers: x-served-pool: hosted-eu-1 and latency 780ms.
routing-bot: Alert: fallback_count[ded-eu-42->hosted] spiked to 127 in last 10m for customer cust-877. Policy: pin_ttl=3600s, last_pin_refresh=1755546400 (expired).
infra_dan: pinging routing service logs, looks like our pin-refresh jobs ran but several refresh attempts returned 503 from the customer auth service (auth timeout), so the router treated the pin as stale and allowed fallback.
customer_ops: but the customer claims they have dedicated capacity reserved and didn't expect fallback to hosted (billing surprise). They have traffic shaping that assumed dedicated-level latency.
billing_rob: @support_jess please cc billing — we already see a +$1.2k spike this hour tied to hosted unit prices. Need to scope credits if we caused unexpected fallback.
support_jess: actionable checklist: 1) reproduce and capture response headers (maya) 2) fix pin refresh failures (infra_dan) 3) stop automatic fallback to non-matching region until pin has been explicitly invalidated (prod change request) 4) communicate to customer and billing.
oncall_maya: repro steps I used: 1) set region param to eu-west-1 2) send 20 requests at t=now 3) observe ~40% go to hosted pools. Attaching sample logs: 
```
[2026-02-14T13:05:12Z] req=r-0a1b2c3e routed_region=eu-west-1 dest=hosted-eu-1 reason=pin_stale_check_failed
[2026-02-14T13:05:27Z] req=r-0a1b2c3f routed_region=eu-west-1 dest=ded-eu-42 reason=ok
```
infra_dan: root cause hypothesis: pin_refresh job depends on auth service; transient auth timeouts cause the router to treat refresh as failed and unset the pin, which allows region-agnostic fallback. We need a conservative fallback policy: if refresh fails transiently, keep existing pin for grace_window (e.g., 5m) instead of immediate fallback.
routing-bot: Proposed mitigation deployed to staging: add grace_window=300s to pin refresh path. Will monitor.
support_jess: customer-facing message draft: "We identified an issue where transient auth timeouts caused your region pin to be treated as expired, allowing requests to fall back to hosted pools. We're rolling a mitigation that keeps pins for an additional 5 minutes when refreshes fail, and we'll review credits for the unexpected hosted usage." Thoughts?
billing_rob: sounds right. Please add concrete number: estimated impacted tokens ~1.1M; propose crediting hosted rate diff ~ $1.2k.
customer_ops: customer accepted the explanation and wants ETA for mitigation. Can we push to prod rollback/patch in next 2h?
oncall_maya: patch is trivial (grace window flag) — need an approval for prod config change. I'm oncall and can run it once infra gives go.
infra_dan: I'll coordinate with eng-release. Raising a hotfix PR now and tagging @eng-sre for fast deploy.
support_jess: keeping this thread linked to ticket #T-4391. I'll update customer every 30m. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
